checks: The scaled argument has derivative ‖uₗ‖/hₗ in the continuous normal direction. Consequently Sₗ integrates 1 and Aₗ/hₗ integrates q over the occupied part of (−1,0), each with factor 1/‖uₗ‖ times tangential area.

A proper limiting cut gives full interval contributions 1 and −1/2. Uniform localization to the limiting projection bounds all strip levels, so null or empty limiting cuts vanish and the relative-boundary remainder on a supporting facet tends to zero.

The global primitive J₁=−Ψ+Ψ²/2 has derivative q on (−1,0), is zero below the ramp and is −1/2 above it. Outside the strip portion is below the roof, yielding −τ+τ²/2. Inside it is above the roof, yielding −τ²/2. Strong L¹ suffices for both squares because 0≤τ≤1.

Adding Sₗ/2 cancels proper contributions and gives −τ(1−τ)/2 outside and +τ(1−τ)/2 inside. Independent exact fraction checks cover points below, inside and above the ramp and both endpoints. The bound χ/4 uses χ=1 on 0<τ<1 and zero partial cost at saturation.

Source 8bc6ff090380166a §5 gives the same J₁ primitive and signed identity through Gauss–Green. The frozen column proof establishes the same cap-wise result and does not assign a sign to the final signed sum.

dependencies.comparison: Same-batch transition theorem supplies this common sequence, the inner-patch one-roof columns, strong L¹ of both selectors, and 1_{0<τ<1}≤χ. The strip proof only uses these pieces with the stated support orientations.

overlap.comparison: Uses the same outward smoothing model with a crude strip-volume bound. It has no signed first moment of the scaled strip and no limiting supporting-facet costs.

readability: The Aₗ/hₗ convention and the distinction between a signed sum and the nonnegative pointwise facet density are explicit.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Normal-column integration gives the two strip moments and the signed partial-capture cost, using the same strongly convergent actual selectors and transition densities.
